title: Scanning troubles / crash on ARM32
body:
### What happened?

After the last update, it's been struggling scanning on some of the more complex folders, and eventually crashing out. I'm open to ideas to help gather more info. I've attached a logfile 

I have been running Syncthing for a year or two on a Drobo5n (3 core ARM32, 768MB ram) tuned for the low specs (Hashers:1 Copiers: 1 comes to mind, among some other little tweaks). I've been able to get some progress by starting with `--paused` and then enabling the folders one by one, but there are two that never finish scanning. After inspecting some more and running the daemon interactively, I see that it eventually crashes.

[syncthing-err.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21796844/syncthing-err.txt)

### Syncthing version

v2.0.1

### Platform & operating system

Linux arm32

### Browser version

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: The output you pasted, and also the attached log, is not in fact the relevant output -- the important bits are at the beginning of the crash log. Can you post a full log please?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: The logs I posted above were with `--audit --auditfile --`. Should I get the logs from --log-level=DEBUG instead?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I think I got it; Let me know if this is complete enough:  [syncthing-err2.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21798015/syncthing-err2.txt)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Yep. You’re running into some thread limit or something. 

```
runtime/cgo: pthread_create failed: Resource temporarily unavailable
SIGABRT: abort

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Is there any config or runtime variable I can tweak to cap the max thread count or curtail subprocesses?
I already have Hashers=1 and Copiers=1 on the folder configs and "Max Folder Concurrency"=1

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: There is not. Typically thread limits are "synthetic", something you can increase if required.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: There are two folders where, even if unpaused alone, the system load goes from 15 to 25 and continues creeping upwards until it eventually crashes. This hasn't happend up until I jumped a few versions. Unfortunate, I may have to restort to rsync for those, or maybe I can slim it down with ignore patterns...

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: From 15 to 25 what? If you think there's a Syncthing problem, please post logs and cpu profiles, or a support bundle which includes both.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I'm speaking of the load average, I believe the number of outstanding processes awaiting execution. 
I have a couple of folders where the scan completes and the load average remains around 6-8. But I have a few that will always kill it, eventually.  I have one going right now, where the load just reached above 20 and the WebUI and api become unresponsive.

I managed to get a response from the /rest/debug/cpuprof endpoint while the load was around 9 and one while it was around 20. It's still running but is unusable.  I'm looking into how to get a more thorough report, now.

[syncthing-cpu-arm32.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21894962/syncthing-cpu-arm32.zip)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Here are go:

[support-bundle-F6PDZJR-2025-08-20T052613.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21896958/support-bundle-F6PDZJR-2025-08-20T052613.zip) 

I had hesitantly disabled fsync to try and relieve some of the pressure, and it has softened the load a bit - it's still trying.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: The only anomalous thing I see in there is that you seem to be running with debug logging of the filesystem package, so that fills log the with mostly useless info while also using unnecessary amounts of CPU. It's using 34 threads, and apparently about 13% CPU at the time of the capture, so load seems to be mostly driven by I/O wait

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hmm, debug logging of the filesystem package where? I'm wondering if that's something I can disable to reduce overhead.
The load has increased to 28 and I tried getting a support bundle, but it's unresponsive.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Recent 2.0 versions are a bit more lean on the memory usage, might be worth a retry.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I'm seeing the same on an rpi 3 and 2.0.11 arm -> windows. Have bumped all ulimits, systemd slice limits, configured for the 'low resources' per docs, set bandwidth limit to 100kb/s even on lan. Initial scan when no sync is setup works fine, but it crashes a few seconds after connecting a remote with empty filesystem. My replication set should be ~15Gb (23k files)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: It is doing the same on my rpi 4 (also 32-bit but 2gb ie 4* the memory of the rpi 3 I was testing on earlier). I feel like there must be a bug in 32-bit (arm?) builds with transferring relatively large numbers of files/folders - perhaps it just requests too much virtual memory or something?
